newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Cricket-India 108-1 at close vs W.Indies' 427.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India 108-1 at close vs W.Indies' 427.

text.p: West Indies, inspired by Carl Hooper's seventh Test century, amassed a total of 427 in the first innings against India who made a strong reply towards the close on the second day of the first Test.
India survived two dropped catches in the first three overs of their innings before progressing to to 108 for one with opener V.V. Laxman completing a half century.
By the close Laxman was 54 not out while partner Rahul Dravid produced a cultured 28 not out in an unbroken second wicket partnership of 76.

Indian leg-spinner Anil Kumble took the last three West Indian wickets to finish with five for 120 off 42.4 overs. Paceman Abey Kuruvilla celebrated his Test debut by claiming three victims at a cost of 82 runs.

West Indies, resuming at 300 for four, dominated the morning session with Hooper and night watchman Ian Bishop adding 57 before Bishop was out for 24, lofting Kumble to deep mid-off where Sunil Joshi took a well-judged running catch.

Hooper began the day on 87 and had needed another 28 minutes to complete his century. He went on to make 129 before being caught by Venkatesh Prasad off Kuruvilla, hitting 17 fours in his 212-ball innnings.
Almost immediately after Hooper's departure, Junior Murray made just one before falling leg before to Kumble on the stroke of lunch with the total on 370 for seven.
After lunch, Kumble wrapped up the innings for 57 more runs.

He had Curtly Ambrose caught at backward point by Saurav Ganguly for 23, Roland Holder caught at slip by Mohammad Azharuddin for 17 and Courtney Walsh bowled for four. Debutant Franklyn Rose was not out 14.
India began shakily and took until the fourth over to get off the mark.
Before this, Navjot Sidhu had been dropped off the inside edge by wicket-keeper Murray off Bishop's bowling while Brian Lara at slip missed an ankle high chance from Laxman's bat in the next over.

Sidhu, on his first overseas tour since he walked out on the squad in England last year, was out leg before for ten off the bowling of Bishop. Television replays suggested the ball may have hit his inside edge first.
After that, the Indians batted with style and increasing conviction.
Scoreboard on the second day of the first Test match between the West Indies and India at Sabina Park on Friday.
Bowling: Prasad 28-5-104-1, Kuruvilla 30-6-82-3, Kumble 42.4-5-120-5, Joshi 27-6-81-1, Ganguly 7-1-17-0, Laxman 3-0-14-0.
Bowling: Ambrose 9-3-13-0, Bishop 10-3-25-1, Rose 6-1-25-0, Walsh 6-0-12-0, Hooper 6-2-20-0, Chanderpaul 4-2-7-0.
